title: Stablecoins Are Becoming Financial Infrastructure — Not Just Crypto Infrastructure
description: Stablecoins have moved from a crypto-trading tool to real payment rails for remittances, payroll, and treasury. Here's what changed, and what hasn't.
excerpt: For most of the past decade, a stablecoin — a cryptocurrency engineered to hold a steady value, typically pegged one-to-one to a fiat currency like the U.S. dollar — existed for one reason: to let traders move in and out of volatile crypto assets without cashing out to a bank account every time. That was the job. It was a trading tool, not a financial system. That framing is out of date. Fintechs are routing cross-border payroll through stablecoin rails. title: Crypto Wallets Are Getting Easier to Use. Is the Seed Phrase Era Ending?
description: How account abstraction, passkeys, and social recovery are replacing the seed phrase as crypto wallets' default onboarding experience, and the tradeoffs.
excerpt: Ask anyone who's tried to get a non-technical friend into crypto what the actual barrier was, and the answer is rarely the technology of blockchains themselves. It's the seed phrase — a sequence of 12 or 24 words generated when a wallet is created, which serves as the master backup for every private key that wallet controls. Lose it, and the funds are gone permanently, with no customer service line to call. title: What Is a Blockchain Node — and Why Does Decentralization Depend on Them?
description: A plain-English explainer on what a blockchain node is, how it differs from a validator or miner, and why node count and distribution drive decentralization.
excerpt: "Decentralized" is one of the most used and least examined words in crypto. Every network claims it. Almost nobody explains what it actually rests on. The honest answer is unglamorous: decentralization is a function of nodes — how many independently operated computers are running a network's software, verifying its rules, and refusing to go along with anything that breaks them.
